history.summary: NOT A HINDU TEMPLE - this is a Presbyterian church. The Sairang Presbyterian Church (Mizoram Presbyterian Kohhran) stands on Sairang Main Road, Tlangnuam, in Sairang - a river-valley town on the Tlawng river about 10-20 km northwest of Aizawl city, historically Mizoram's river port and now the terminus of the Bairabi-Sairang railway line (verify exact distance and local church history). It belongs to the Mizoram Presbyterian Church Synod, the largest Christian denomination in Mizoram: the Synod traces its origin to 11 January 1894 and the Foreign Missionary Society of the Calvinistic Methodist Church (the Welsh Presbyterian mission; Presbyterians in the north, Baptists in the middle of Mizoram). Headquartered at Mission Veng, Aizawl, it reported about 628,719 members and 588 ministers in 2023 (verify), and is a constituent of the Presbyterian Church of India. As with Mizo kohhran (congregations) generally, the church serves as the social as well as spiritual hub of the locality - Sunday worship, Sunday School, women's fellowship (Kohhran Hmeichhia), youth fellowship (Kristian Thalai Pawl) and choirs structure weekly community life. Note: several Presbyterian congregations exist in Sairang (including Sairang Vengthar and Sairang Dinthar), so this record should be verified against the specific Sairang Main Road church (verify).

name: Sairang Presbyterian Church
town_description: Aizawl is the capital and largest city of Mizoram, spread across steep ridges about 20 km from the Assam border. Sairang, where this church stands, is a town on the Tlawng river on Aizawl's northwest fringe - historically the river port through which goods reached the hills, and now the rail terminus of the Bairabi-Sairang line (verify). Almost entirely Christian, Aizawl's public life is organised around its churches; the Mizoram Presbyterian Church Synod headquarters is at Mission Veng, Aizawl.
